rule: One colour forms several identical copies of a shape, and another colour forms a single odd shape with the same box size. In the output every copy's box holds the odd shape in the odd colour, and the odd shape's box holds the repeated shape in the repeated colour.
scope: Repeated-versus-odd shape exchange on 7..30 canvases, with edge-spanning binary masks 2..6 per side and 2..10 copies. Random sampling mixes loose and tight non-overlapping placements. A local mask-frequency check enforces a uniquely identifiable repeated template. Dimensions, foreground colours, mask sizes and copy count are explicit optional controls.

authored_scope: Supported: box sizes 2..4 by 2..4; shapes that may be disconnected but touch all box edges; 2..6 copies; random grid size 7..18 per side; random distinct colours on a 0 background. Not supported: more than two foreground colours, shapes of different box sizes, overlapping boxes, and (in random scenes) copies touching or nearly touching, which the fixtures do show.
authored_constraints: The repeated and odd masks differ, and each touches all four edges of its h x w box.
The repeated colour's total cell count exceeds the odd colour's count, so the odd shape is the minority colour.

In random scenes every pair of boxes is separated by at least max(h,w)-1 (at least 1) background rows or columns. Then no shifted window can mimic a copy, and the repeated pattern is the unique most frequent template.
The two colours are distinct, non-zero and differ from the background 0.
The output always differs from the input because the masks differ and the colours swap.
